articles.title: Hamstring lengthening for crouch gait in ambulatory cerebral palsy: a systematic review of surgical extent, technique, durability and harms.
articles.authors: Khatri JP, Shibu MK, Parmar RS, Ghosh AK, Gopinathan NR, Kanwat H, et al.
articles.population: Children with ambulatory cerebral palsy undergoing hamstring lengthening for crouch gait
articles.outcomes: Popliteal angle, knee flexion at initial contact, stance knee flexion, functional gains, recurrence, overcorrection, nerve palsy
articles.take_home: Hamstring lengthening can improve knee angle measurements in crouch gait, but functional improvements are inconsistent and often reduce as children grow. Surgery should only be done after careful assessment and families should understand that benefits are uncertain and there are risks including nerve damage and overcorrection.

articles.title: Long-Term Shoulder Outcomes Following Tendon Transfers for Brachial Plexus Birth Injuries.
articles.authors: Grove LG, Varas-Rodriguez E, Shaughnessy W, Pulos N
articles.population: Children aged 5 years or younger with brachial plexus birth injury
articles.outcomes: Modified Mallet scores for shoulder abduction, external rotation and hand-to-mouth movement; active external rotation; external rotation at 90 degrees; forward flexion; revision rates
articles.take_home: Tendon transfer surgery significantly improved shoulder function in children with brachial plexus birth injuries, with improvements lasting an average of 8.7 years after surgery. Revision surgery was needed in only 2.4% of patients, suggesting the procedure provides lasting benefits.

articles.title: Radiographic Mid-Thigh Girth, a Proxy for Body Habitus, Correlates With Patient-Reported Outcomes More Strongly Than Limb Alignment Parameters in Children With Lower Limb Differences.
articles.authors: Sang L, Kwok V, Wang S, Sabharwal S
articles.population: Children aged 8 to 18 years presenting for surgical reconstruction of lower-limb differences
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcomes using Limb Deformity-Scoliosis Research Society (LD-SRS) and PROMIS-25 questionnaires; radiographic parameters including limb alignment, joint angles, and mid-thigh girth
articles.take_home: Standard measurements of limb alignment on X-rays showed little connection to how children felt about their condition, but body size measurements (mid-thigh girth and BMI) were linked to worse patient-reported pain, function and quality of life. Body habitus should be considered when discussing treatment options with families.

articles.title: Self-Reported Psychological Distress in Adolescent and Young Adult Idiopathic Scoliosis Patients Undergoing Posterior Spinal Fusion.
articles.authors: Barnhill K, Qiu A, Hassan F, Lenke LG, Caccappolo E, Eisler L
articles.population: Adolescents and young adults aged 11 to 26 with idiopathic scoliosis undergoing posterior spinal fusion
articles.sample_size: 103 patients with preoperative assessments; 78 completed follow-up at 6 weeks
articles.outcomes: Preoperative rates of self-reported depression (27%) and anxiety (52%); postoperative improvements in anxiety scores and self-image; worsening in function and pain scores; higher baseline anxiety and depression associated with worse postoperative functional and self-image outcomes
articles.take_home: More than half of young people preparing for spinal fusion surgery report anxiety or depression before surgery, which is much higher than clinical diagnoses suggest. Whilst anxiety improved after surgery, those with higher anxiety and depression before surgery had worse pain, function and body image concerns in the short term after their operation.

articles.title: Retinoblastoma.
articles.authors: Toumasis PN, Chantada GL, Corson TW, de Graaf P, Gerrish A, Kaliki S, et al.
articles.outcomes: Biology, diagnosis, treatment, survivorship, and global health equity
articles.take_home: Retinoblastoma is largely curable but outcomes vary greatly worldwide, with the worst results in poorer regions. New treatments focusing on saving the eye and new diagnostic methods using liquid biopsy show promise, but ensuring access to these advances remains a global priority.

articles.title: Perioperative respiratory adverse events in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy with laryngeal mask airway versus endotracheal tube ventilation: multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: Han Y, Yi X, Xia J, Zhang W, Zhao Z, Zhu N, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 2-7 years undergoing adenotonsillectomy under general anaesthesia
articles.sample_size: 400 children (200 in laryngeal mask airway group, 200 in endotracheal tube group)
articles.outcomes: Perioperative respiratory adverse events including laryngospasm, bronchospasm, desaturation, airway obstruction, severe cough, and stridor
articles.take_home: Children who had a laryngeal mask airway during adenotonsillectomy had fewer breathing problems (22.5%) compared to those with an endotracheal tube (57.5%), with the biggest difference in coughing and breathing difficulties after surgery. No serious complications occurred in either group.

articles.title: Hidden Economic and Social Costs of Clubfoot Treatment Using the Ponseti Method in Indiana.
articles.authors: Alkhatib N, Moore MM, Upadhyay K, Loder RT, DeLeon GA, McCaffrey CJ, et al.
articles.population: Children with talipes equinovarus (clubfoot) treated with the Ponseti method in Indiana
articles.sample_size: 165 patients (74 in retrospective part, 91 in prospective part)
articles.outcomes: Travel distances, non-insured costs, household income percentage, appointment changes, family impacts including childcare arrangements and hotel stays
articles.take_home: Families treating clubfoot in Indiana face substantial hidden costs averaging around £2000-£2700 in non-insured expenses and must travel over 900 miles on average for appointments. Many families need to arrange childcare or bring other children to appointments, highlighting the significant financial and social burden of clubfoot treatment in the United States.

articles.title: Comparative Outcomes of Pinning Versus Permanent Fixation for Adolescent Supracondylar Humerus Fractures.
articles.authors: Rakowski DR, Lalka A, McKeever J, Johnson T, Sibbel SE
articles.population: Children and adolescents aged 10 to 17 years with extra-articular supracondylar humerus fractures
articles.outcomes: Time to bone union, elbow range of motion, nerve deficits, heterotopic ossification
articles.take_home: Permanent fixation resulted in slightly better elbow movement than pinning alone, but this difference is unlikely to matter in practice. Both treatments had similar healing times, nerve problems and bone complications, though older adolescents and more severe fractures took longer to heal regardless of treatment type.

articles.title: Casting Without Reduction Versus Reduction With or Without Fixation for Mildly Displaced Pediatric Distal Radius Metaphyseal Fractures: A Randomized Noninferiority Trial.
articles.authors: Garcia-Rueda MF, Mendoza-Pulido C, Gil-Laverde JFA
articles.population: Children aged 5 to 10 years with mildly displaced distal radius metaphyseal fractures
articles.sample_size: 60 children randomised (59 with primary outcome data)
articles.outcomes: Upper-extremity function at 6 months measured by PROMIS Pediatric Upper Extremity T-score; adverse events
articles.take_home: In children with mildly displaced wrist fractures, simply putting the arm in a cast without reduction under anaesthesia worked just as well as reduction with anaesthesia, with better safety as there were no serious complications in the cast-only group compared to 2 complications in the reduction group.
